# Rummikub Starting Hand Simulation

```{r}


set.seed(67) #my dopamine receptors are fried

# Deck: 1 Pair 1-13 in 4 colors + 2 jokers = 106 tiles
colors <- c("red", "blue", "yellow", "black")
tile_deck <- c()
for(color in colors) {
  for(number in 1:13) {
    tile_deck <- c(tile_deck, paste(color, number))
    tile_deck <- c(tile_deck, paste(color, number))
  }
}
tile_deck <- c(tile_deck, "red_joker", "black_joker")#jokers

```

# Simulation

```{r}
n<-1000
#Simulate
result <- do(n)*{
  hand <- sample(tile_deck, 14, replace = FALSE)#Draw 14 at Start
  jokers <- sum(hand %in% c("red_joker", "black_joker"))#Joker Count 
  pairs <- sum(table(hand) >= 2) #duplicate count
  c(jokers = jokers, pairs = pairs)#dataframe
}

```

# Results

```{r}

mean(result$jokers >= 1)#P(at least one joker)
mean(result$jokers == 2)#P(both jokers)
mean(result$pairs >= 1)#P(at least one pair)

```

# Visualizations

```{r}
hist(result$jokers, main = "Jokers per Starting Hand", xlab = "Number of Jokers")
hist(result$pairs, main = "Duplicate Pairs per Starting Hand", xlab = "Number of Pairs")

```

# Intial Hand Simulation and Statistics

```{r}

set.seed(67) # after all why not

# Create full deck of 106 tiles
simulate_initial_hand <- function() { 
 
  colors <- rep(c("Red", "Blue", "Yellow", "Black"), each = 26) # 13 numbers × 2 copies=26 per suit
  numbers <- rep(rep(1:13, each = 2), 4) # Two copies of each number for each color
  jokers <- rep("Joker", 2)
  joker_colors <- rep("Joker", 2) #no color associated
  joker_numbers <- rep(NA, 2) #no number associated

  full_deck <- data.frame(
    color = c(colors, joker_colors),
    number = c(numbers, joker_numbers),
    tile_id = 1:106
  )
  
# Draw 14 tiles for initial hand
  hand_indices <- sample(1:106, 14, replace = FALSE)
  initial_hand <- full_deck[hand_indices, ]
  
  return(initial_hand)
}

n_simulations <- 1000
all_simulations <- do(n_simulations) * {
  hand <- simulate_initial_hand()
  
# Calculate statistics for this hand
  num_jokers <- sum(hand$color == "Joker")
  num_numbers <- sum(!is.na(hand$number))
  avg_number <- mean(hand$number, na.rm = TRUE)
  
#Color Checking
  has_red <- any(hand$color == "Red" & !is.na(hand$number))
  has_blue <- any(hand$color == "Blue" & !is.na(hand$number))
  has_yellow <- any(hand$color == "Yellow" & !is.na(hand$number))
  has_black <- any(hand$color == "Black" & !is.na(hand$number))
  colors_present <- sum(c(has_red, has_blue, has_yellow, has_black))

#Final Dataframe
  data.frame(
    jokers = num_jokers,
    avg_number = avg_number,
    colors_count = colors_present
  )
}

#Result(head)
head(all_simulations)

```


```{r}

# RUMMIKUB TILE DRAW SIMULATION

# Simulate drawing 14 tiles from 106 tile deck
set.seed(67) # after all why not

tile_sim <- do(1000) * {
  # Draw 14 random tiles from 106
  hand <- sample(1:106, 14, replace = FALSE)
  
  # Count jokers (tiles 105-106 are jokers)
  jokers <- sum(hand >= 105)
  
  # For numbered tiles (1-104), calculate average number
  numbered_tiles <- hand[hand <= 104]
  tile_values <- ((numbered_tiles - 1) %% 13) + 1  # Convert to 1-13
  avg_number <- mean(tile_values)
  
  data.frame(jokers = jokers, avg_number = avg_number)
}

# Results
mean(tile_sim$jokers)
sd(tile_sim$jokers)
mean(tile_sim$avg_number)

# Visualizations
gf_bar(~jokers, data = tile_sim, fill = "steelblue") %>%
  gf_labs(title = "Jokers in Initial Hand", x = "Number of Jokers", y = "Count")

gf_histogram(~avg_number, data = tile_sim, bins = 15, fill = "darkred") %>%
  gf_labs(title = "Average Tile Number", x = "Average Number", y = "Frequency")

```
